groups.sentence: Instructors base AI rules on their existing collaboration norms and tell students how AI fits within them.
Students treat generative AI use like assistance from another person when the instructor has given no guidance on AI.
Students treat the use of AI as they would treat assistance from another person.
Students complete each assignment without substantive assistance from others, including automated tools.
Students follow existing ethical scholarship, plagiarism and citation rules for AI use, citing and quoting AI sources like any other source.
Students may use AI for anything they are allowed to do with another person, such as discussing work or generating ideas.
Students do not use AI in any way that would count as plagiarism or unauthorized help if a human did it.
Uncited or unacknowledged use of another's work, whether a person or AI, is an academic integrity violation.
AI is analogous to a person, collaborator, classmate or knowledgeable friend whose help is treated like human help.
Plagiarism and academic integrity rules apply to AI-generated content and sources just as to human ones.
